Petroleos de Venezuela SA Posts Steady Output and Revenue Growth in Latest Results

Petroleos de Venezuela SA (PDVSA) reported stable production levels and a modest increase in annual revenues in its latest financial disclosure, reflecting a year of cautious operational management and gradual recovery for the Venezuelan oil sector.

According to company figures released on Tuesday, crude oil output for the calendar year reached an average of 785,000 barrels per day, up from 744,000 barrels per day in the previous year. The state-owned oil producer also reported annual revenues of $21.7 billion, marking a 6.3% increase year-on-year, buoyed by sustained export volumes and an uptick in global oil prices.

Company president Ricardo Melendez attributed the positive results to ongoing efforts to optimize operations and bolster efficiency across PDVSA’s core production regions. “These results reflect the hard work of our teams and our commitment to stabilizing production,” Melendez said in a statement. “We are prioritizing investments in key fields and infrastructure to ensure consistent output and to strengthen our role in supplying energy both domestically and to our export partners.”

Industry analysts noted that PDVSA’s performance comes amid persistent challenges faced by the Venezuelan oil sector, including aging infrastructure and the need for technology upgrades. However, the improved figures suggest a degree of resilience. “The incremental growth in output and revenues is a positive sign,” said Laura Rodríguez, energy analyst at the Caracas-based consultancy Andes Energy Insights. “While the industry still faces significant structural hurdles, these results indicate that PDVSA is making measured progress in stabilizing operations and maximizing available resources.”

Exports remained the primary driver of revenue growth, with the company reporting shipments to traditional markets in Asia and Latin America. Domestic supply levels were maintained, with PDVSA fulfilling its commitments to local refineries and downstream partners, including Orinoco Petrochemicals and Caribbean Energy Partners.

Union representatives echoed the company’s emphasis on operational stability. “Our members are committed to supporting the company’s recovery,” said Miguel Fernández, spokesperson for the National Federation of Oil Workers. “We continue to work closely with management to ensure safe and reliable operations.”

Looking ahead, PDVSA has indicated plans to further invest in enhanced oil recovery techniques and targeted maintenance programs. The company also cited ongoing collaborations with service providers to address logistical bottlenecks and improve supply chain efficiency.

Trade body sources said the results would bolster confidence among sector stakeholders. “PDVSA’s steady performance is welcome news for the domestic industry,” said Carmen Silva, executive director of the Venezuelan Oil Producers Association. “Continued operational discipline will be key to sustaining this momentum in the coming year.”
